speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when you first noticed this lesion on your leg and whether it has changed in size or appearance since then?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and diabetes, I need to know if you have experienced any systemic symptoms like fever, chills, or joint pain recently? Also, has the lesion developed a central crust or necrotic center, and is it significantly more painful than a typical insect bite?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a painful, necrotic ulcer with purplish borders at the site of a minor trauma (pathergy), alongside your history of Crohn's disease, is highly suggestive of Pyoderma Gangrenosum. I will proceed with a tissue biopsy to rule out infection and confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Histopathology shows neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.
